project.name: Kingsgate Place Office Development
project.sponsor: Tom Ashworth, Development Director, Aldermoor Estates

lines.note: Secant pile wall, two-level basement and raft. Obstruction breakout and extra dewatering on dayworks.
Fixed-price order placed October 2025; includes metal decking and stairs.
Unitised curtain wall. Paid through a project bank account from July 2026.
Includes lifts, BMS and the substation fit-out.

lines.category: Internal finishes and Cat A fit-out
lines.note: Raised floors, ceilings and core finishes. Tenant changes on levels 7-10 not yet priced.
Site management, welfare, hoarding, tower crane TC1 and scaffold.
Architect-led design team novated to the contractor at contract signature.
Released in June for weekend steel erection shifts and an extended mobile crane hire.

notes.author: R. Okafor
notes.text: Obstruction breakout in the north-east corner is being recorded on dayworks sheets against SUB-01. Not yet valued.

notes.author: S. Carter
notes.text: Contingency release for weekend steel erection shifts and the extended mobile crane hire approved by the client at the 12 June progress meeting.

notes.author: Commercial team
notes.text: Project bank account opened for Vitrana Facades. From July, curtain wall payments go through the PBA and not direct to the subcontractor.

notes.author: R. Okafor
notes.text: Substructure final account agreed with Groundline. SUB-01 closes above its line budget.

risks.title: Unrecorded below-ground obstructions in the north-east corner
risks.description: Piling hit the brick foundations of former Victorian warehouses and a disused culvert that the site investigation did not show.
risks.mitigation: Probing ahead of the piling rig; rig resequenced to other areas while obstructions were broken out on dayworks.

risks.title: Groundwater higher than the site investigation predicted
risks.description: Groundwater stood about 1.5 metres above the level in the site investigation report, flooding the basement excavation after heavy rain.
risks.mitigation: Four additional deep wells installed. Dewatering switched off once the basement raft and walls were complete in May.

risks.title: Structural steel delivered late by Brennan Steel Fabrications
risks.description: A shortage of heavy column sections at the mill delayed first steel by five weeks. Liquidated damages are 45,000 per week beyond the contract completion date.
risks.mitigation: Recovery plan approved 12 June: weekend erection shifts, a second mobile crane, and columns resequenced so floors 1-6 could be erected first.

risks.title: Curtain wall subcontractor in financial distress
risks.description: Vitrana Facades asked for accelerated payment terms and missed a payment to its aluminium extrusion supplier in May.
risks.mitigation: Project bank account in place from July; vesting certificates held for units fabricated off site; parent company guarantee requested.

risks.title: Tower crane downtime from winter wind
risks.description: TC1 is out of service above 38 mph. The programme allowed eight lost days over the winter.
risks.mitigation: Critical lifts moved to early mornings; five days lost against the eight allowed.

risks.title: Substation energisation date not confirmed by the network operator
risks.description: The regional distribution network operator has not confirmed an energisation date for the new 1,500 kVA substation. Commissioning cannot start without it.
risks.mitigation: Temporary generator strategy costed for commissioning; monthly escalation through the client's utilities adviser.

risks.title: Building control approval of revised slab-edge fire-stopping
risks.description: Changing the curtain wall bracket changed the fire-stopping detail at the slab edge. Building control has not yet approved it.

risks.title: BREEAM Excellent credits at risk from embodied carbon
risks.description: Swapping in heavier column sections to cover the mill shortage raised embodied carbon above the figure assumed at design stage.
risks.mitigation: Life-cycle assessment being rerun. Low-carbon concrete specified for the upper floor slabs to compensate.

risks.title: MEP second-fix labour shortage over the winter
risks.description: Halden needs 42 electricians at peak from November. It has 28 committed, and two other city-centre projects are recruiting for the same trades.
risks.mitigation: Second electrical subcontractor gang being procured; prefabricated riser modules to reduce on-site labour.

risks.title: Anchor tenant change requests on levels 7-10
risks.description: Lorimer Hale LLP asked for a deeper raised-floor void, two extra risers and a revised reception on level 7.
risks.mitigation: Two of five changes instructed with agreed costs; three still with the client for review.

risks.title: Crane oversail licence with the adjoining owner
risks.description: TC1's jib passes over the neighbouring Corn Exchange Chambers, so a licence is needed to oversail.
risks.mitigation: Oversail licence signed in January with a slewing restriction outside working hours.

risks.title: Facade visual mock-up rejected under the planning condition
risks.description: The planning officer rejected the first visual mock-up panel because the vertical fins looked too shallow from street level.
risks.mitigation: Deeper fin profile approved at the second mock-up on 19 June; planning condition 14 discharged in July.

risks.title: Steel price escalation before the order was placed
risks.description: Section prices rose through the summer of 2025 while the frame design was being finalised.
risks.mitigation: Fixed-price order placed with Brennan in October 2025 at tender rates.

reports.author: Siobhan Carter
reports.executive_summary: At the end of its second quarter on site, Kingsgate Place is on programme. The secant pile wall around the basement is complete, and bulk excavation has reached formation level on the southern half of the site. Piling in the north-east corner hit the foundations of former Victorian warehouses and a disused culvert that the site investigation had not shown. The rig was moved to other areas while these were broken out, so the overall programme lost no time, but the breakout is being paid on dayworks. Groundwater is about 1.5 metres higher than the site investigation predicted, and four more deep wells have been installed. Steel fabrication drawings are 80% approved, and first steel is due on site on 18 May.
progress: Secant pile wall complete: 214 piles. The final pile was cast on 6 March after the obstruction breakout.
Bulk excavation to formation level on grids A-F; the first basement raft pour is booked for mid-April.
Tower crane TC1 erected and passed its thorough examination on 9 February.
Oversail licence with Corn Exchange Chambers signed in January.
Curtain wall visual mock-up panel ordered from Vitrana Facades for May.

milestones.name: Secant piling complete
milestones.comment: Final pile cast 6 Mar; resequencing absorbed the delay.

issues: The north-east corner obstruction breakout is being paid on dayworks and has not yet been valued, so the substructure cost is being watched closely.
The network operator has still not confirmed an energisation date for the new substation.
next_period: Pour the basement raft and start the core walls.
Receive first steel on 18 May and start frame erection from grid A.
Build and present the curtain wall visual mock-up to the planning officer.
reports.budget_note: Contract sum under the design and build contract signed September 2025.
reports.forecast_note: Assumes obstruction costs stay within the substructure allowance.

reports.author: Siobhan Carter
reports.executive_summary: Kingsgate Place is red this quarter. First steel from Brennan Steel Fabrications arrived five weeks late because the mill ran short of heavy column sections. The frame is now five weeks behind the erection programme, which puts the June 2027 practical completion date at risk. Vitrana Facades, the curtain wall subcontractor, has asked for accelerated payment terms and missed a payment to its extrusion supplier in May, and we are treating this as financial distress. The client approved a recovery plan on 12 June. It uses contingency to fund weekend erection shifts and a longer mobile crane hire, and aims to top out the frame by 11 September. The basement structure is complete and dewatering has been switched off.
progress: Basement raft, walls and ground-floor slab complete; dewatering switched off on 29 May.
First steel delivered on 22 June against a planned 18 May; erection started on grid A the same week.
Second curtain wall visual mock-up approved on 19 June with a deeper fin profile.
Recovery plan approved by the client: weekend erection shifts, a second mobile crane, and floors 1-6 erected first.
issues: The steel frame is five weeks behind the erection programme.
Vitrana Facades' finances are a threat to the whole envelope package; a project bank account is being set up.
Lorimer Hale LLP has raised five change requests for levels 7-10. None has been priced yet.
next_period: Run weekend erection shifts through August and top out by 11 September.
Open the project bank account for Vitrana and take vesting certificates for units fabricated off site.
Price the Lorimer Hale change requests and put them to the client.

reports.author: Siobhan Carter
reports.executive_summary: The project is back to amber. The steel frame topped out on 4 September. The recovery plan won back two of the five weeks lost, so practical completion is now forecast for 16 July 2027, three weeks after the contract date of 25 June 2027. The substructure final account was agreed in August and closes above its line budget because of the obstruction breakout and the extra dewatering. It is the only cost line forecast to overrun. Vitrana Facades is now paid through a project bank account, and curtain wall installation started on level 1 on 7 September. The main risk to the new date is a shortage of MEP second-fix labour over the winter.
progress: Steel frame topped out on 4 September, a week ahead of the recovery plan target.
Substructure final account agreed with Groundline on 21 August.
Curtain wall installation started on level 1 on 7 September; 38 of 612 units installed.
MEP first fix under way on levels 1-3; riser modules for levels 4-11 ordered prefabricated.
Two of the five Lorimer Hale change requests instructed with agreed costs.

milestones.name: Substation energisation
milestones.comment: Date still unconfirmed by the network operator.

issues: The employer's agent rejected the extension-of-time claim for the steel delay, so liquidated damages apply to the three-week slip unless more time is recovered.
Building control has not yet approved the revised slab-edge fire-stopping detail.
Three Lorimer Hale change requests are still with the client, so the fit-out scope is not fixed.
next_period: Close the envelope up to level 6 by the end of November.
Bring in a second electrical subcontractor gang before second fix starts in November.
Escalate the substation energisation date through the client's utilities adviser.
reports.budget_note: Includes the substructure final account agreed on 21 August.
reports.forecast_note: Excludes liquidated damages and the unpriced tenant changes.
